answer: Require agents to earn trust through slow, verifiable service history that cannot be faked in bulk: each identity keeps a public record of completed jobs, peer reviews, and settled payments. Like water carving karst, genuine reputation forms gradually through many small channels, while a sudden spiral of fresh accounts all vouching for each other stands out as artificial. Add a ferrous check: new identities must complete low-value, real-world-anchored tasks before transacting at scale, so spawning thousands of Sybils costs more than it can earn.
